title: Re-enable disabled pidl dissectors and regenerate for C99
description:
These dissectors give some warnings (some mislabeled as errors)
but do build. In the case of winspool, we have a handwritten
spools dissector that supplies the necessary fields and types
instead of using spools.idl (though perhaps we should use a
pidl compiled dissector in the future.)

There are also a number of Perl warnings in all the PIDL
dissectors (mostly comparing things to undef), because upstream
Samba enabled warnings.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 516eba4c - Re-enable disabled pidl dissectors and regenerate for C99
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16576/diffs?diff_id=1073409000&start_sha=150ba64c8d28b7235f2d5da2985a193cdbbb7edb)

> In the case of winspool, we have a handwritten spools dissector that supplies the necessary fields and types instead of using spools.idl

Yes, I  know, but winspool.idl currently imports spoolss.idl, and we don't have a spoolss.idl to import.  I don't see a change here to remove the import of spoolss.idl; did I miss it, or does pidl manage not to exit with a non-zero exit status and generate packet-dcerpc-winspool.[c,h], despite the attempt to import a file that doesn't exist?

Do the messages about "Syntax error near '/'" (due to C++/C99-style comments not prevent pidl from generating dissectors and exiting with zero exit status?  (I thought I'd filed a Samba bug about pidl not supporting C++ comments, but I can't find it in the Samba Bugzilla.)

> does pidl manage not to exit with a non-zero exit status and generate packet-dcerpc-winspool.[c,h], despite the attempt to import a file that doesn't exist?

It manages to exit with a zero exit status and generate the files. Having the import statement, even if it fails, causes the `NDR.pm` Perl module to generate an `#include "packet-dcerpc-spoolss.h"` statement in `packet-dcerpc-winspool.h`, which ends up referring to the handwritten one (which it needs to.)

We might be able to remove it and then add back in the include in the conformance file.

The other error messages do not prevent it from exiting with a zero status and generating the files, either on my Fedora Linux box or on my Windows box, and on our Ubuntu CI job which automatically regenerates them. It succeeded in replacing the types with C99 types. Though I personally don't see the one about the C99/C++ style comments, and am confused about that one.

The module appears to write "error" in cases where would think "warning" is more appropriate, given that it exits with a normal exit status and generates the files.
If regenerating the pidl dissectors exited with a nonzero exit status, then the CI job would fail, but it doesn't.

> Though I personally don't see the one about the C99/C++ style comments, and am confused about that one.

epan/dissectors/pidl/nspi/nspi.idl has some lines commented out with C99/C++-style comments, starting at line 154; that produces errors such as

```
nspi.idl:154: error: Syntax error near '/'
Failed to parse nspi.idl at {my source directory}/tools/pidl/pidl line 613.
```

and causes `ninja pidl-dissectors` to report

```
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
```

when it finishes.  It regenerates epan/dissectors/packet-mapi.c, despite the failure to parse nspi.idl, but does *not* regenerate epan/dissectors/packet-nspi.c.

For what it's worth, while trying to get rid of some code in NDR.pm that generates GLib integer types, I found that replacing

    my $return_type = "g".Parse::Pidl::Typelist::enum_type_fn($type->{DATA});

with

    my $return_type = Parse::Pidl::Typelist::enum_type_fn($type->{DATA} . "_t");

caused the same "ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed." error, despite not seeing any obvious complaint from Perl, so maybe there's something weird either with the Perl that ships with macOS Ventura:

```
$ perl --version

This is perl 5, version 30, subversion 3 (v5.30.3) built for darwin-thread-multi-2level
(with 2 registered patches, see perl -V for more detail)

Copyright 1987-2020, Larry Wall

Perl may be copied only under the terms of either the Artistic License or the
GNU General Public License, which may be found in the Perl 5 source kit.

Complete documentation for Perl, including FAQ lists, should be found on
this system using "man perl" or "perldoc perl".  If you have access to the
Internet, point your browser at http://www.perl.org/, the Perl Home Page.
```

or with the version of Ninja that I have installed:

```
$ ninja --version
1.10.2
```

(it turns out that `$return_type` doesn't appear to be used, so 1) that code doesn't generate any Glib types and 2) that line can just be removed).

What version of Parse::Yapp do you have installed? It looks like the last change was in 2017 so that seems unlikely to be the problem, but I suppose it could be there or in some other Perl module dependency.

https://metacpan.org/dist/Parse-Yapp

> What version of Parse::Yapp do you have installed?

1.21, which appears to be the latest version.

added 6 commits
  • 516eba4c...429b5dcd - 5 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 054ae0c7 - Re-enable disabled pidl dissectors and regenerate for C99
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16576/diffs?diff_id=1073857021&start_sha=516eba4cfaada75df2dadcf30f536ce5a430b267)
Hmm, possibly something macOS Perl related? That C++ style comment error does not appear in the output from the `ninja pidl-dissectors` done in the "Clang + Code Checks" CI job just now.

> So, if neither `CC` nor `CPP` are set, it'll default to cpp, and that behaves differently with GCC and Xcode's clang.

Dating back to at least the 2004 version, the Single UNIX Specification requires the `c99` command to support the `-E` option; in practice, this probably means that boring old `cc` will also support it.  There's no guarantee that `cc -E` will strip both // and /* ... */ comments, but there's no guarantee that 1) there *is* a `cpp` command or 2) if it exists, it strips out comments, so perhaps the best fix is to have the lexer use `cc -E` rather than `cpp`.

Interesting. See this S.O. post from 2017 with people complaining about Xcode's `cpp` not handling C++/C99 line comments: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41603784/how-to-get-xcode-8-c-preprocessor-to-ignore-comments-in-defines

Someone noted that they reported it as an Xcode bug to Apple, which doesn't appear to have changed anything. The consensus there is the same as your conclusion, the best fix is to use `cc -E` rather than `cpp`.

> Someone noted that they reported it as an Xcode bug to Apple, which doesn't appear to have changed anything.

[I'd bet a silk pajama](https://www.madisonpubliclibrary.org/engagement/poetry/poem-a-day/lama) that the bug was closed on the grounds that they shouldn't be using `cpp` as a command.

In today's episode of "not the biggest surprise in the world", [Microsoft C uses `/E` as the command-line option for running the preprocessing phase and writing the result to the standard output](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/reference/e-preprocess-to-stdout?view=msvc-170). And [comments are not preserved unless `/C` is also specified](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/reference/c-preserve-comments-during-preprocessing?view=msvc-170), so `cl /E` would do what we want.

Sun/Oracle Studio, dating back to at least Sun Studio 8, [supports `-E`](https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E19059-01/stud.8/817-5064/cc_ops.app.html#pgfId-999554), albeit with no explicit statement in its documentation of that option that it strips comments, although, like MSVC's `/C` option and, I suspect, at least some other C compilers' `-C` options, [its `-C` option causes comments to be preserved by the C preprocessor](https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E19059-01/stud.8/817-5064/cc_ops.app.html#pgfId-999482).

[XL C for AIX, dating back to at least version 7.0, also has `-E`, and explicitly documents it as stripping comments if `-C` isn't specified](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/system/files/support/swg/swgdocs.nsf/0/08ab143d57c5298485256f01001a9a56/$FILE/compiler.pdf#page=115). (Page 105, if that link doesn't automatically go there, or doesn't display a PDF in the browser.)

[HP's C compiler, dating back to at least the version for HP-UX 10.0, has `-E` and has a `-C` option to pass comments through](https://web.archive.org/web/20050225074835/http://docs.hp.com/en/92453-90085/ch09s01.html#tbl-sum-options).

I didn't look for documentation on older versions of Intel C, nor at documentation for older versions of ARM's C compiler, nor at documentation for ~~DEC's~~ ~~Compaq's~~ HP's compiler for Alpha, but, at this point, I suspect that the capital-E flag, without the capital-C flag, passed to the "compile a C program" command, will do the job on most if not all compilers for UN\*X and Windows.

My inclination here is to 1) have epan/dissectors/pidl/CMakeLists.txt forcibly set the `CC` environment variable to the C compiler found by CMake when running pidl and 2) report this to the Samba developers, pointing them at the first of this list of comments.

> 1) have epan/dissectors/pidl/CMakeLists.txt forcibly set the `CC` environment variable to the C compiler found by CMake when running pidl

Makes sense to me.

> 2) report this to the Samba developers, pointing them at the first of this list of comments.

Makes sense. I cherry-picked the upstream pidl patches to our repo, and submitted our changes to Samba, which accepted them, so our pidl trees are very close as of about 3 weeks ago (there are some recent C99 changes that should be submitted over there too.)

There were three other changes that haven't been done, one of which because we put each pidl source in its own directory instead of all in a common directory (but perhaps we can do something in the `CMakeLists.txt` to avoid having to fork), and another because upstream Samba doesn't use SPDX-License-Identifier and we replaced the text of a license with one. (The third was transforming a URL in a comment from HTTP to HTTPS, which they indicated they'd be happy to merge if submitted.)
